title: Telnet service exposed
description: Telnet transmits the entire session, including credentials, without encryption. Any host on the path can capture or modify it.
remediation: Disable the Telnet service and replace it with SSH. If legacy equipment requires Telnet, restrict it to a dedicated management VLAN behind a jump host.

title: FTP service exposed
description: FTP sends credentials and file contents in cleartext and is frequently misconfigured to allow anonymous access.
remediation: Replace FTP with SFTP or FTPS. If FTP must remain, enforce TLS and restrict source addresses.

title: Cleartext mail retrieval protocol exposed
description: POP3 and IMAP without TLS expose mailbox credentials to network interception.
remediation: Disable the cleartext listeners and require POP3S (995) / IMAPS (993) with modern TLS only.

title: rsh/rlogin/rexec service exposed
description: The legacy r-services authenticate using trusted-host files and send credentials in cleartext. They are trivially abused for lateral movement.
remediation: Disable rsh, rlogin and rexec entirely; use SSH with key-based authentication.

title: TFTP service exposed
description: TFTP has no authentication and is commonly used to pull device configurations, including credentials.
remediation: Disable TFTP unless a device strictly requires it, and then restrict access to the management network only.

title: MySQL/MariaDB reachable from the network
description: A database port is reachable over the network. Database services should not normally be exposed beyond the application tier.
remediation: Bind the database to localhost or the application subnet and enforce firewall rules. Require strong per-application credentials and audit accounts for weak or shared passwords.

title: PostgreSQL reachable from the network
description: A PostgreSQL port is reachable over the network. Database services should not normally be exposed beyond the application tier.
remediation: Restrict listen_addresses and pg_hba.conf to application hosts, place the service behind a firewall and enforce scram-sha-256 authentication.

title: Microsoft SQL Server reachable from the network
description: A SQL Server port is reachable over the network, exposing the authentication surface and the UDP browser service that enumerates instances.
remediation: Disable the SQL Browser service, restrict the TCP endpoint to the application subnet and disable the built-in sa account.

title: Redis reachable from the network
description: Redis ships without authentication by default. A reachable instance commonly allows arbitrary command execution via configuration rewrite.
remediation: Bind Redis to localhost or a private interface, enable requirepass with a strong secret, enable protected-mode and run the process as an unprivileged user.

title: MongoDB reachable from the network
description: Older MongoDB deployments default to no authentication. Internet-reachable instances are routinely copied wholesale by automated crawlers.
remediation: Enable authentication and role-based access control, bind to a private interface and restrict access with firewall rules.

title: Elasticsearch reachable from the network
description: Elasticsearch historically shipped without authentication. A reachable cluster exposes all indexed data and often supports scripting-based command execution.
remediation: Enable security features, require authentication and TLS, and never expose the transport or HTTP port to untrusted networks.

title: Memcached reachable from the network
description: Memcached has no authentication and has been widely abused for reflection-amplification DDoS and cache data disclosure.
remediation: Bind Memcached to localhost or a private interface, disable UDP and enforce firewall rules.

title: Cassandra reachable from the network
description: A Cassandra native transport or Thrift port is reachable, exposing the cluster and its data to unauthenticated or weakly authenticated access.
remediation: Restrict cluster ports to cluster nodes and application hosts, and enable the Cassandra authenticator and authorizer.

title: CouchDB reachable from the network
description: CouchDB administrative endpoints allow database creation and query execution. Exposed instances expose all resident data.
remediation: Bind to a private interface, require authentication and disable the admin party configuration.

title: SMB file sharing exposed
description: SMB is reachable from an untrusted network. Historically this has exposed the service to wormable remote code execution and to relay attacks when signing is not enforced.
remediation: Block SMB at the network perimeter, require SMB signing, disable SMBv1 and remove anonymous share access.

title: NetBIOS name service exposed
description: NetBIOS name and datagram services leak host and domain information and enable spoofing attacks.
remediation: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP where it is not required and block the ports at the perimeter.

title: Remote Desktop Protocol exposed
description: RDP reachable from an untrusted network is a primary initial-access vector for ransomware operators, through both credential attacks and pre-auth vulnerabilities.
remediation: Place RDP behind a VPN or a zero-trust gateway, enable Network Level Authentication, enforce account lockout and MFA, and restrict source addresses.

title: VNC service exposed
description: VNC is reachable from the network and frequently protected only by a short, brute-forceable password.
remediation: Tunnel VNC over SSH or a VPN, require a strong password and bind the listener to localhost.

title: WinRM management endpoint exposed
description: WinRM provides remote command execution and should not be reachable from untrusted networks.
remediation: Restrict WinRM to management hosts, prefer HTTPS (5986) and require strong authentication.

title: Docker daemon API exposed
description: An unauthenticated Docker API grants effective root on the host: containers can be created that mount the host filesystem.
remediation: Never expose the Docker socket or TCP API. Use TLS client certificates if remote access is unavoidable, and restrict access with firewall rules.

title: Kubernetes API server exposed
description: A Kubernetes API endpoint is reachable from an untrusted network. Misconfigured anonymous authentication or weak RBAC turns this into full cluster compromise.
remediation: Restrict API server access to trusted networks, disable anonymous authentication and audit RBAC bindings for cluster-admin grants.

title: Kibana reachable from the network
description: Kibana exposes indexed log and application data and has a history of unauth access when placed directly on the internet.
remediation: Place Kibana behind authentication and a reverse proxy, and restrict source networks.

title: Apache Solr reachable from the network
description: Solr's admin interface allows configuration changes that have repeatedly led to remote code execution when exposed.
remediation: Restrict the admin interface to trusted hosts and enable authentication on the Solr instance.

title: ZooKeeper reachable from the network
description: ZooKeeper has no authentication by default and arbitrary clients can read or modify coordination data.
remediation: Restrict ZooKeeper to cluster members and enable SASL authentication with ACLs.

title: rsync daemon exposed
description: An rsync daemon reachable from the network may publish modules read-write without authentication.
remediation: Disable the rsync daemon in favour of rsync over SSH, or restrict hosts allow/deny and require module authentication.
